findings: Inspected all 11 exact decoded samples: frame 0, frame 8 (nearest to .25 s), .5 s, first displacement peak, 1 s/reaction, free-foot search, placement, foot approach, transition midpoint, macro and final frame; plus decoded contact sheet. Tool supports sequential frame inspection, not continuous video playback.

First-second deck/support changes are present against relatively steady London background. Human root follows support before delayed torso/arm compensation; motions are deliberately restrained. Owner playback must determine whether instability and causal ordering read immediately enough.

Clothing, hair, shoes, rails and lighting retain frozen identities. No per-frame provider generation, AI morph model or temporal structural hallucination is introduced. Controlled UV deformation changes pixels/shape locally; this is authored distortion, not a recovered 3D scene.

No hard alpha-card edges, exposed inpainting gaps or obvious mask halos were identified in sampled frames. Early test detected a local deformation foldover; widened mask falloff fixed sampled orientation tests across the opening. Mild texture stretch around the body/foot remains a method limitation, requiring owner motion review.

Planted sole/adjacent support track within the tested displacement bound; source contact shadows/reflections remain present. No detached floating person identified in samples. Small free-foot lift is illustrative; the frozen starting stance already contains raised-heel/toe contact. The proof does not recreate a full realistic walk cycle.

Camera push deliberately crops upper body and later the free foot while bringing the planted shoe forward. No transparent exposed frame edge identified. This is intentional shot reframing; platform/device crop validation remains future work.

Macro transition uses a short optical dissolve with visible double exposure at midpoint. Foot scale is closer after camera adjustment, but back-to-side shoe angle and scene geometry differ between the two fixed sources. This continuity limit is explicit; owner should judge whether the transition feels coherent at normal speed.

Macro keeps physical shoe/deck detail, small surface motion and delayed correction; no force rings, giant arrows, final captions or narration/audio are used. Required simplified-model/motion-exaggerated disclosure is readable throughout.

Local media checks pass at 1080×1920, 30 fps, 180 frames, six seconds, H.264/yuv420p and no audio stream. Entire MP4 decodes without errors. No Meta geometry/device evidence, full production, locked-master or publication approval is implied.
method: Inspected exact decoded MP4 frame samples and contact sheet; full decode checked separately. Tool inspection is sequential frames, not continuous video playback.
